kjv: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward
mine: I am your shield; your reward will be very great
note: Hebrew sekharkha harbeh me'od can be a second predicate ("[I am] your very great reward") or a separate clause ("your reward [will be] very great"); the Masoretic accents and harbeh (an infinitive "greatly") favour the latter.
Hebrew ben-mesheq beti is obscure (mesheq occurs only here, with a pun on Dammeseq); v. 3 makes clear the point is inheritance, but "steward" and "heir" are both guesses.

kjv: a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp
mine: a smoking firepot and a flaming torch
note: Hebrew tannur is a portable clay oven or firepot and lappid a torch; "furnace" and "lamp" suggest the wrong objects.
